items.title: (b) String Plucked at Quarter Length (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: (b) String Plucked at Quarter Length: a main subheading of 7.5 Stationary waves on a stretched string, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 147-147.

blocks.text: Agar wohi string apni length ke ek chauthai (quarter) hisse se chhedi jaye to phir stationary waves banti hain, jin ke nodes aur antinodes Fig. 7.7 (b) mein hain. Ab string do loops mein vibrate karti hai. Yeh case is liye banta hai ke string ko antinode wali jagah se chheda gaya. Do consecutive nodes ka faasla aadhi wavelength hai, is liye string ki length l is mode ki wavelength ke barabar hai. Agar in waves ki wavelength λ₂ ho to:

blocks.alt: Wohi jakra taar do loops mein jhoolta hai, Double loop: dono siron aur beech mein node N, har loop mein antinode A; neeche l = lambda2 = 2(lambda2/2).
blocks.caption: Figure 7.7(b): Vibration ka doosra mode (kitab ki Figure 7.7(b) ke mutabiq asal khaaka).

blocks.title: Diagram ko samjhein
blocks.text: Do consecutive nodes ka faasla aadhi wavelength hai. Ek loop mein l = λ₁/2; do loops mein l = 2(λ₂/2) = λ₂. Speed v dono mein barabar hai, is liye doosre mode ki frequency pehle ki double hai: f₂ = 2f₁.

λ₂ = l ko λ₁ = 2l (Eq. 7.2) se milayein to pata chalta hai ke is case mein wavelength pehle case ki aadhi hai. Eq. (7.3) batati hai ke waves ki speed string ke tension aur mass per unit length par depend karti hai, chhedne ki jagah par nahi. Is liye dono cases mein speed v barabar rehti hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab λ₂ = l ko bhi number (7.4) deti hai, halanke yeh number pehle f₁ = (1/2l) √(F/m) ko mil chuka hai; is ka apna naya number hona chahiye. Kitab likhti hai “Eq. (7.4) ko Eq. (7.1) se milayein”; pehle case ki wavelength wali equation λ₁ = 2l asal mein Eq. (7.2) hai (Eq. 7.1 to v = fλ hai). Kitab speed ke liye “Eq. (7.2)” likhti hai; speed wali equation v = √(F/m) asal mein Eq. (7.3) hai.
